'''Natalia Pasternak Taschner''' (born 15 May 1976) is a Brazilian [[microbiologist]], author, and [[Science communication|science communicator]].<ref>[https://bv.fapesp.br/en/pesquisador/43749/natalia-pasternak-taschner/ Natalia Pasternak Taschner] – website of [[São Paulo Research Foundation]]</ref> She is the first president of the [[Instituto Questão de Ciência]] (IQC) (English: Question of Science Institute). She was director of the Brazilian arm of the [[science festival]], [[Pint of Science]] (2016–2019), columnist for the Brazilian national newspaper "[[O Globo]]", for [[The Skeptic (UK magazine)|The Skeptic magazine]] (UK), and Medscape (WebMD).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Natalia Pasternak Taschner {{!}} Columbia SIPA |url=https://www.sipa.columbia.edu/faculty-research/faculty-directory/natalia-pasternak-taschner |access-date=29 September 2022 |website=www.sipa.columbia.edu |archive-date=29 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929014209/https://www.sipa.columbia.edu/faculty-research/faculty-directory/natalia-pasternak-taschner }}</ref> She also hosts two weekly radio shows "The hour of Science" at Brazil's [[Central Brasileira de Notícias|CBN]] national radio station. Taschner is also the publisher of [[Brazil]]'s first magazine on critical thinking, Revista Questao de Ciencia.{{R|Questão de Ciência 2020}}

She contributes as a visiting professor at the Public Administration School at Fundação Getúlio Vargas, São Paulo, as well as a research collaborator at the University of São Paulo. She is the first Brazilian to be named a fellow of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry|Committee for Skeptical Inquiry (CSI)]] in the United States. She has received numerous other awards and recognitions.

[https://www.editoracontexto.com.br/produto/ciencia-no-cotidiano-viva-a-razao-abaixo-a-ignorancia/2788127 Science in our Daily Lives], which received Brazil's National Literature prize for best science book in 2021 ([https://www.premiojabuti.com.br/premiados-por-edicao/premiacao/?ano=2021&eixo=03b7f793-10a1-eb11-b1ac-002248374496 Prêmio Jabuti)], and [https://papirus.com.br/produto/contra-a-realidade-a-negacao-da-ciencia-suas-causas-e-consequencias-2/ Against Reality: Science Denialism, Its Causes and Consequences], are two of her books on science popularization. She is the only Brazilian on the BBC's list of the 100 most influential women in 2021,<ref>{{Cite news |title=BBC 100 Women: quem está na lista de mulheres inspiradoras e influentes de 2021 |language=pt-BR |work=BBC News Brasil |url=https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/internacional-59561198 |access-date=29 September 2022}}</ref> and she is now an Adjunct Senior Research Scholar at Columbia University's Center for Science and Society, thanks to Professor Stuart Firestein's offer.<ref name=":0" /> Her research focuses on ways to enhance science communication and battle denial and disinformation, as well as bringing scientific thought to future policymakers and assisting in the establishment of a worldwide partnership for evidence-based global policies.

== Education and career ==
Born into a Jewish family,<ref>{{cite web |title=O Holocausto e a Cloroquina |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/opiniao/o-holocausto-a-cloroquina-24532831 |website=O Globo |access-date=28 March 2021 |language=pt-BR |date=15 July 2020}}</ref> Natalia Pasternak Taschner is daughter of university professors Mauro Taschner and Suzana Pasternak.<ref>{{cite web |title="Se seguir o que Bolsonaro recomenda, vou morrer" |url=https://valor.globo.com/eu-e/noticia/2020/12/11/a-mesa-natalia-pasternak-se-seguir-o-que-bolsonaro-recomenda-vou-morrer.ghtml |website=Valor Econômico |access-date=28 March 2021 |language=pt-br |date=11 December 2020}}</ref> Pasternak entered the [[University of São Paulo]] (USP) in 1998 and received her [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in Biological Sciences in 2001. She subsequently obtained a PhD degree in Biological Sciences (Microbiology) in 2006 from the Institute of Biosciences of the University of São Paulo (IBS-USP), with the thesis entitled ''The regulation of [[alkaline phosphatase]] by the [[sigma factor]] S of [[RNA polymerase]] from [[Escherichia coli]]''.<ref>[http://lattes.cnpq.br/2971054847583007 CV Natalia Pasternak Taschner] – website of the [[National Council for Scientific and Technological Development]]</ref> From 2007 to 2013 she completed a post-doctorate in microbiology, in the field of [[molecular genetics]] of bacteria at the University of São Paulo.{{R|group=|QUBES2018|page1=|q1=|3=}}

Pasternak founded the science blog ''Café na Bancada'' (English: "Coffee on the Lab Bench"){{R|SiM}}, with the mission statement: "Difundir a ciência com café!" (English: "Spread the science with coffee!"). The website is defunct but continues as a blog, started in 2015, on Facebook. Pasternak became director of the Brazilian arm of [[Pint of Science]] from 2015 to 2019, in which she coordinated scientific lectures in bars in more than 50 cities in Brazil.{{R|IQC|QUBES2018|SiM}} As of 2020, Pint of Science was being managed by Luis Gustavo Almeida.{{R|PoS BR}}

In 2018 she became the first president of the Instituto Questão de Ciência, (IQC) an organisation focused on the defense of scientific evidence used in public policies.{{R|group=|SiM|page1=|q1=|SI 2018|Globo2018|EXAME2018}} Pasternak went as far as to invest her own money into the formation of the IQC, making her the second philanthropist in Brazil to invest private money in science communication.{{R|Alves}} IQC is a co-organizer, along with Aspen's [[Office for Science and Society]], of the 2020 "Aspen Global Congress on Scientific Thinking and Action" in [[Rome]].{{R|Aspen}}

Early in 2020 Pasternak organised the first specialization course in the public communication of science in the city of São Paulo. The course aims to train journalists and other communication professional about the dissemination of science.{{R|Unesp}}

Pasternak has been made a Fellow of the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]] in 2020.{{R|Fellow}} Since September 2021, Pasternak has been a visiting scholar at [[Columbia University]]'s Center for Science and Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Visiting Scholars {{!}} Science and Society |url=https://scienceandsociety.columbia.edu/content/visiting-scholars |access-date=27 March 2022 |website=scienceandsociety.columbia.edu}}</ref>

== Activities ==
[[File:Natalia Pasternak Taschner CSICon 2018 Politicization of Science- CAMs in the Brazilian Public Healthcare System.jpg|thumb|Natalia Pasternak Taschner [[CSICon]] 2018 Politicization of Science CAMs in the Brazilian Public Healthcare System]]
{{BLP sources section|date=April 2020}}
Taschner has been involved in many activities related to the promotion of science, and attended several conferences and seminars including:
* Taschner has contributed to the [[Genetic Literacy Project]] on the fear of biotechnology, GMO mosquitos, and opposition to pesticides.{{R|Genetic Literacy Project}}
* Taschner presented "Politicization of Science: CAMs in the Brazilian Public Healthcare System" at [[CSICon#Sunday Morning Papers Session|CSICon]] 2018{{R|CSICon|SiM}} and "Brazilians Love and Support Science! Or is it Pseudoscience?" at CSICon 2019.
* In 2019 she organised a cycle of seminars about ignorance, in partnership with the University of São Paulo{{R|IEA USP 2019}}
* In 2018 she presented "How to spread science in Brazil" at the Academic Congress of Uncisal
* Taschner exhibited at the International Day of Light in 2018 at the [[UNESCO]] headquarters in Paris.
* She had an exhibition at the 61st anniversary of the [[Professor Aristóteles Orsini Planetarium|Planetarium]] in São Paulo, 2018.
* In 2017 she participated in "4º Fala Ciência – Curso de Comunicação Pública de Ciência e Tecnologia" promoted by [[Federal University of Viçosa|Universidade Federal de Viçosa]]{{R|UFV}}
* She presented a [[TED (conference)|TEDx USP Talk]] titled "A ciência brasileira e Síndrome de Cassandra" (English: Brazilian science and Cassandra syndrome){{R|UFV2|SiM}}
* In 2016, Taschner was involved in the Brazilian National Science and Technology Week festival
* In 2008, Taschner participated in the "XII International Congress of Bacteriology and Applied Microbiology" in [[Istanbul]]. She presented a paper entitled ''The Xanthomonas axonopodis citri PHO regulon''.

== Presence in media ==
Most media relating to Taschner can be found on the IQC website.{{R|Clippings}} In 2020 Taschner co-authored an article with Carlos Orsi for ''Skeptical Inquirer'' entitled ''"Believing" In Science Is Not "Understanding" The Science: Brazilian Surveys''.{{R|SI2020}}

Taschner appeared in the journal ''Skeptic'' in 2018 with an article entitled "Brazilian Cancer Quackery".{{R|Skeptic}}

Taschner has been interviewed on several occasions, including:
* Friends of Science in Medicine interviewed her for the April 2019 edition.{{R|SiM}}
* [[Susan Gerbic]] interviewed Taschner for ''[[Skeptical Inquirer]]'' in the lead-up to CSICon 2018.{{R|SG2018}}
* [[Stuart Vyse]] interviewed Taschner for the Jan/Feb 2020 edition of ''Skeptical Inquirer''.{{R|Vyse 2020}}
* Rob Palmer interviewed Taschner at CSICon 2019 for [[Richard Saunders (skeptic)#Podcasting|''The Skeptic Zone'']] podcast, episode 756.{{R|SZ}}
* Brian Kirby interviewed Taschner at CSiCon 2019 for ''502 Conversations''.{{R|Kirby}}
* ''[[Science Magazine]]'' quoted her in an article about the risk of reducing rigor in testing [[hydroxychloroquine]] for treatment of [[COVID-19]].{{R|AAAS}}
* [[Cara Santa Maria]] interviewed Taschner for her podcast, ''Talk Nerdy''.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://www.carasantamaria.com/podcast/natalia-pasternak |title=Brazilian Pseudoscience w/ Natalia Pasternak |website=Talk Nerdy |publisher= |host=Cara Santa Maria |date=4 October 2021 |time= |access-date=23 October 2021}}.</ref>
Taschner has lectures at ''Casa do Saber'' on "What is Science and why trust it?",{{R|CoS1}} "Brazilian Science: Unknown to Brazilians"{{R|CoS2}} and the [[Anti-vaccine activism|anti-vax movement]].{{R|CoS3}}

Several of Taschner's lectures and presentations are available on YouTube, including:
* ''Follow the opening of the academic semester of UnB with the biologist Natalia Pasternak.''{{R|UNB}}
* ''Stand Up Scientists{{halfspace}}!''{{halfspace}}{{R|USP}}
* ''Conversations with Scientists''{{R|CNR}}
* ''Brazilian scientists and Cassandra's syndrome''<ref>{{Cite AV media|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F3kUeDlP3Io|title=A ciência brasileira e a síndrome de Cassandra|date=2018|last=Pasternak|first=Natalia|type=TEDxUSP|language=pt}}</ref>
